why: I checked every verifier PASS/FAIL condition against its expect line. None is stricter than its line. No check asks for exact error wording ("non-empty error message"), a branch-name rule, a mutation test or a limit on which files the PR may touch. The extras (shebang, mode 100755, lockfile, CRLF) are marked "Advisory (not a pass/fail condition)". Every behaviour line is checked by running something. Checks 1–2 run the CLI on temp files and look at stdout, stderr and exit codes. Check 3 imports lint and calls it. Check 4 runs `npm test` in the package as well as reading the test files. Check 6 runs `npm ci && npm test` and queries the workflow run. Check 5 only reads files, but its line is about files existing, not about runtime behaviour. The builder brief adds details such as engines and a bin entry, but these are build instructions, not pass conditions.
